text:
Maya: quick heads-up — FairShare detector fired for org=org-742 at 1799012338, but the signal looks weird. :thinking:
Liam: can you paste the raw metric window?
Maya: pasted below — short bursts across ~120 keys, each under 5 req/s, but 95th token rate spiked for the org.
Maya: `org_rate/second{org_id="org-742"} -> 620 req/s (1m)`
Arjun: that pattern often means many small clients doing sync calls vs one noisy tenant. Our per-key limiter would be fine but org-level bumped the org.
Megan: user reported customer impact — they saw throttling during ML batch jobs. We need a way to avoid penalizing many low-volume API keys vs a true noisy neighbor.
Liam: agree. Proposal: add a heuristic that looks at keys_active_count + key_rate_stddev. If keys_active_count > X and per-key median < Y, ignore org-level ejection and prefer per-key smoothing.
Arjun: sketch of heuristic: 
```
if keys_active_count > 30 and median(key_rate) < 3 req/s:
  apply per_key_smoothing(window=30s, decay=0.5)
else:
  apply_org_eject()
```
Maya: love the idea. Two follow-ups: how do we avoid oscillation (flip-flop) when traffic transitions from many small clients to one heavy key?
Liam: add hysteresis and a cooldown: require the org_eject_condition to hold for 3 consecutive windows (30s each) before enforcing org-eject. Also exponentially backoff un-eject.
Megan: from product POV we need visibility in the console: show "FairShare decision" with contributing signals (keys_active_count, median_key_rate, top_key_share). Operators should be able to override per-org.
Arjun: agree — expose flags: `org_fairshare_mode: auto|enforce|observe` in console and API. Default `auto` will run detector and decide.
Maya: telemetry queries we'll need for postmortems. Example PromQL to surface the signals: 
```
sum by(org_id) (rate(requests_total[1m])) as org_rps
count by(org_id) (requests_total{job="api"}) as keys_active_count
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by(le, org_id)(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m]))) as median_latency
```
Liam: also add a top-k per org share metric so we can say "top key accounts for 60% of tokens". If top_key_share > 0.4 -> favor org eject.
Megan: UX note — when auto-eject triggers, show a non-blocking banner and a link to a debug page that lists top keys (masked), recent spikes, and a one-click "request temporary capacity" flow.
Arjun: implementation-wise: change detector service (routing) -> emits decision + rationale event to event-stream. Rate-limiter picks up decision, console subscribes for visualization.
Maya: what about rollout? risk is false positives causing customer perf regressions. I'd like a canary: 1) observe for 48h with logging only, 2) dark-launch enforcement for 1% of orgs, 3) ramp.
Liam: operational playbook: when quota-bot flags repeated org_fairshare anomalies, on-call gets an automated slack thread + link to the debug page.
quota-bot: [alert] FairShare anomaly detected: org=org-742, score=0.87, action=observe -> https://console.internal/redwood/fairshare/org-742
Megan: wording for console: call it "FairShare protection" (not "smoothing") — less jargon for customers.
Arjun: small nit — metric cardinality: tracking top-k per org will add cardinality. We'll compute top-k in routing node and emit aggregated annotation, not raw per-key timeseries.
Maya: ok next steps action items: 
- Arjun: implement detector change + rationale events (owner)
- Liam: add cooldown/hysteresis to limiter (owner)
- Megan: mock console panel + wording (owner)
- Maya: run 48h observe canary on 5% of traffic, then dark-launch enforcement for 1% (owner)
Liam: putting a PR label on this now.
Arjun: will open a draft RFC with tests and perf targets.
Maya: thanks — tagging @SRE in case we need emergency rollback hooks :eyes: 
Liam: noted.
Maya: resolved for now, will follow up with RFC link. :thumbsup:
